# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**Rowan Carter**
[Street address]
[City], Missouri [ZIP]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Aetna — Member Complaint and Appeal Unit
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
Fax: 859-425-3379

**RE:** Appeal of denial dated August 19, 2026
**Member:** Rowan Carter
**Member ID:** W914903090
**Reference number:** POC-5BA41AD17E-24277
**Service denied:** Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446
**Plan:** Aetna (Commercial/ACA), Missouri
**Governing policy:** Aetna CPB 0660 – Knee Arthroplasty (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0660.html)

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) that my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, requested for me. Your notice of August 19, 2026 states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking Aetna to reconsider that decision, because the criteria published in Aetna's own policy — Aetna CPB 0660 – Knee Arthroplasty — line up closely with what is already in my medical records.

Below, I have set out the plan's criteria in the plan's own words, followed by what my records show for each one.

## 1. Pain and functional disability interfering with activities of daily living

The plan's policy states:

> "Pain and functional disability that interferes with ADLs due to osteoarthritis or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee joint; and"

My records establish this. I have had nine months of progressive knee pain that is not relieved by rest. I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake three to four times a night because of the pain.

## 2. Physical examination findings

The plan's policy states:

> "Limited range of motion, crepitus, or effusion or swelling of knee joint on physical examination: and"

My examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. I note that this criterion, as published, ends in a colon and appears to introduce a list of conditions that was not reproduced in the material available to me. If Aetna applied any additional exam requirement under this heading, I ask that it be identified specifically so that it can be addressed.

## 3. Arc of motion

The plan's policy states:

> "Patient's knee arc of motion (full extension to full flexion) is not limited to 90 degrees or less; and"

My examination notes that my range of motion is limited by pain. The measured arc of motion in degrees is recorded as [measured arc of motion in degrees, from Dr. Marchetti's exam note]. I ask that this measurement be obtained from my treating surgeon's records rather than treated as absent.

## 4. Radiographic evidence, single compartment

The plan's policy states:

> "Radiographic evidence of moderate/severe osteoarthritis (i.e., Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 3 or 4) (see Appendix ) affecting only a single (medial, lateral or patellofemoral) compartment of the knee joint; and"

My records establish this directly. MRI of the knee dated June 9, 2026 shows full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially. That is Grade 4 disease in a single compartment — the medial compartment — which is precisely what this criterion describes, and it is why a partial (rather than total) replacement was requested.

## 5. Unsuccessful conservative therapy

The plan's policy states:

> "History of of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management; 12 or 24 weeks depending on age/BMI) that is clearly addressed in the medical record (see Note Footnote3 *** ) with at least half of the necessary conservative therapy consisting of formal physical therapy (in-person with a licensed physical therapist as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy)."

And:

> "Physical therapy needs to be confirmed either by the actual PT notes, or by documentation in the member claims history."

My records establish this. I completed **14 weeks** of supervised physical therapy with a licensed physical therapist, from April 10, 2026 through July 17, 2026, attending **16 visits**. This was in-person, formal physical therapy — not home or virtual — and it is documented in my physical therapy discharge note, which is the form of confirmation the policy itself calls for. My age is [age] and my BMI is 29. If Aetna concluded that my course of conservative care was insufficient, I ask that the specific basis for that conclusion be identified in writing so that it can be addressed.

The policy also lists the components of that conservative management:

> "Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics; and"

I took NSAIDs for eight months with inadequate relief.

> "Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises; and"

My supervised physical therapy was focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion.

> "Supervised physical therapy (activities of daily living [ADLs] diminished despite completing a plan of care); and"

This describes my situation exactly. I completed the plan of care — 16 visits over 14 weeks, through discharge — and my activities of daily living remain diminished: I still cannot climb stairs without assistance and still wake three to four times nightly in pain.

> "Activity modification; and"

If Aetna requires separate documentation of activity modification beyond what appears in my physical therapy and office records, I ask that this be stated so my surgeon's office can supply it.

The policy makes assistive devices and injections optional for members without relative contraindications:

> "Assistive device use (required for persons with relative contraindications Footnote4 † to joint replacement, optional for others); and"

> "Therapeutic injections into the knee (required for persons with relative contraindications Footnote4 † to joint replacement, optional for others)."

Even though the policy treats injections as optional for members in my situation, I had one anyway: a corticosteroid injection on June 17, 2026, which gave me only about two weeks of partial relief.

Finally, the policy itself recognizes that conservative care has limits in a knee like mine:

> "Conservative therapy may be inappropriate for severe osteoarthritis with bone-on-bone articulation in the weight-bearing portion of the joint (medial and/or lateral but not patello-femoral); and"

My MRI documents bone-on-bone apposition in the medial compartment — a weight-bearing compartment, and not the patellofemoral compartment. I nonetheless completed 14 weeks of formal physical therapy, eight months of NSAIDs, and an injection before surgery was requested.

## 6. Ligament stability

The plan's policy states:

> "Member must have intact, stable ligaments, in particular the anterior cruciate ligament; and"

My surgeon's examination and MRI report address ligament integrity. The specific finding is [ligament/ACL status as stated in Dr. Marchetti's exam note and the June 9, 2026 MRI report]. I ask that this be confirmed from those records.

## 7. Diabetes and co-morbidities

The plan's policy states:

> "If member is diabetic, their hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) should be less than 8 percent within 3 months prior to knee arthroplasty."

And:

> "For members with significant conditions or co-morbidities, the risk/benefit of unicompartmental knee arthroplasty should be appropriately addressed in the medical record."

My diabetes status is [diabetic status; HbA1c value and date if applicable]. My records do document that I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

---

## What I am asking

The denial notice tells me that my request does not meet the plan's medical necessity criteria, but it does not tell me which criterion in CPB 0660 was found unmet or what evidence was missing. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is needed, and the records in the prior authorization packet already speak to the criteria Aetna publishes.

I respectfully ask Aetna to:

1. **Overturn the denial** and authorize the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446); or
2. If the denial is maintained, **identify in writing the specific criterion or criteria from Aetna CPB 0660 – Knee Arthroplasty that were found unmet**, the records reviewed, and exactly what additional documentation would satisfy them, so that my surgeon's office can provide it.

I also request the credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made this determination, and I ask that this appeal be reviewed by a physician with experience in orthopedic surgery.

I am submitting this appeal using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form, available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals. I understand from my denial notice that **my appeal must be received by February 15, 2027** (180 days from the August 19, 2026 date of notice), and I am sending it by fax to **859-425-3379** and/or to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, which I understand to be the authoritative address. I can also be reached through Aetna Member Services at 1-800-872-3862 or the number on my card.

Please note that the policy excerpts quoted above are the only portions of CPB 0660 available to me; the policy contains additional provisions and appendix material I have not quoted, and I have not quoted the denial notice as a statement of the plan's criteria. My records are current as documented by my treating providers, and I am glad to authorize release of any additional records needed.

Thank you for reviewing this appeal.

Sincerely,

**Rowan Carter**
Member ID: W914903090
Reference number: POC-5BA41AD17E-24277
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date signed]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated August 19, 2026
- Physical therapy discharge note (April 10, 2026 – July 17, 2026, 16 visits)
- MRI report dated June 9, 2026
- Office notes from Dr. Marchetti, orthopedic surgery
- Injection record dated June 17, 2026
- [Any additional records provided by my surgeon's office]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
